notes: Direct HTTP fetch worked throughout (no block encountered; robots.txt has no Claude-specific disallow). Method: checked main nav/mega-menu (homepage href scrape), collections.json (750 collections across 3 pages), sitemap_collections_1.xml, then opened every candidate and confirmed exact qty via exhaustive products.json enumeration (paginated limit=250, deduped by product id) -- this matched the site's own rendered 'You've viewed X of Y products' text on every page where that text was present, confirming collections.json's own products_count field is inflated/unreliable (consistent with prior project finding) and was NOT used for qty. Two collections are in main navigation: /collections/best-selling-product (title 'Bestsellers | Top Kitchen Essentials Shop') and /collections/loved-by-customers (title 'Loved by Customers', matches the 'Customer Favorites' target term) -- these are the confident, canonical rows. Four additional bestseller-named collections exist on the site (found via sitemap, not nav) with genuinely distinct product sets (low overlap vs the canonical listing, so not aliases) but unclear whether the site actively surfaces them anywhere in the UI -- flagged for human review rather than silently excluded or silently included. EXCLUDED (not emitted as a row): /collections/wc-bestsellers, title 'WC Bestsellers', rendered 'of 1101 products' -- verified via /collections/all/products.json enumeration that 1101 is the site's ENTIRE product catalogue count; this is a mislabeled catch-all collection, not a genuine bestseller curation, so it fails the 'genuinely represents a bestseller/popularity merchandising concept' test in section 3 of the brief.
